about: What a device can do for a person, in the words every Poolhouse interface shows. A use is listed only when it works. Each use has one action per state: 'open' names a screen, 'panel' a tab on it, 'install' asks for the named libraries first (the computer fills the names, and 'sources' when no download source is chosen yet), 'copy' is text to put on the clipboard. 'view' is the screen the use needs; an interface without that screen leaves the use out. The computer answers GET /ui/device-uses with these words filled in.
limit: One AI model, or one training run, always stays on one computer. Poolhouse does not split either one across computers.

this_device.heading: What this computer can do
this_device.intro: Nothing has to be running first. Each box says what it needs.
this_device.note: Your other computers cannot yet send this one chat, files, training or other jobs. The one exception is for developers: running project tests, once it is set up.

uses.title: Keep AI models
uses.summary: Download models and store them here, ready to start later.

empty.detail: Nothing downloaded yet. Free space: {free} GB.

uses.title: Train a small model of your own
uses.summary: Teach a new model from your own text, or to sort text into categories.

install.detail: Needs the training tools, about {size} MB. They download from the internet when you choose this.

internet_off.detail: Needs the training tools. Allow internet downloads in Settings first.

uses.title: Run long jobs in the background
uses.summary: Training and other long jobs wait their turn here. You can watch or stop them.

uses.title: Turn speech into text
uses.summary: Write out what is said in a recording, on this computer.

ready.detail: The speech engine is working. It is run from the Tools screen, which is made for developers.

uses.title: Chat with a model
uses.summary: Ask questions and get answers from a model running on this computer.

needs_model.detail: Choose one and Poolhouse downloads it.

uses.title: Compare models
uses.summary: Measure how well and how fast your models answer.

ready.detail: Each model is started while it is measured.

uses.title: Let a guest ask your model
uses.summary: A guest can ask your shared model questions, and nothing else: no files, projects, jobs or settings on this computer.

ready.detail: You set their limits and can remove them with one click. Poolhouse does not save or show what they send, but whoever controls this computer could still read it.

other_device.heading: What you can do with {name} from here
other_device.choose: What you can do with it
other_device.intro: This list is only what works from this computer today.
other_device.note: Chat, copying models and files, training, comparing models, speech and other jobs cannot be sent to {name} from here yet. To use it for those, open Poolhouse on {name}.

uses.title: Run project tests on it
uses.summary: For developers: projects that use Poolhouse's test runner.

developer.detail: Works after it is turned on, on both computers. {name} also needs Python 3.13 and a copy of Poolhouse's source code.

action.label: Copy a request for your coding agent
action.copy: Set up Poolhouse remote tests (docs/test-farm.md) so that the device {own} can run project tests on the device {device}.

adding.title: What another computer adds
lines: From this computer you cannot yet send it chat, files, training or other jobs. Open Poolhouse on it to use it for those.
For developers: project tests can run on it, once that is set up.
